title: acme-orders, mapped
subtitle: What acme-orders does, where it starts, where its data goes, and what to know before changing it, read from the code at f36ec1c.

verdict.text: acme-orders is a small Python CLI that imports the Acme tea shop's daily `;`-separated order export, prices each order, stores it in SQLite, can mail receipts and serves a read-only order API. Finance's month-end job reads `orders.total_cents` straight from the SQLite file. Before changing anything: since 2026-10-02 the daily import in the local log copy has exited with an error. Commit 49bc16d removed decimal-comma parsing and its test, and the shop's export contains prices like `12,50`. [high]

blocks.text:
Order intake for the Acme tea shop. Every morning it imports the shop's order export (CSV, `;` separated), prices each order (discount code, then 20% VAT, rounded once per order) and stores it in SQLite. The shop's admin panel reads single orders over a read-only HTTP API. [high] The code does all of this (`importer.py`, `pricing.py`, `storage.py`, `server.py`); that the admin panel is the caller comes from `docs/api.md:3` only [med].

Users: the morning import job, the shop's admin panel, and finance. Finance's month-end job reads `orders.total_cents` from a nightly copy of the SQLite file and sums it per day (`docs/finance-export.md:3`). Only the docs say this [med].

sections.title: Flows
sections.intro: I read every hop marked [high]. Hops marked [med] come from docs or the log, not from code.

blocks.title: 1. Daily import: export CSV → SQLite → finance

items.title: Cron starts the import
items.text: A host cron runs `acme-orders import` at 06:00 against `/srv/acme-orders/data/orders-<date>.csv`. The cron is not in the repo. [med]

items.title: CLI loads settings
items.text: `load_settings()` reads `acme.yaml` from the current directory if it exists, then env overrides; gives `db_path` (default `acme.db`). [high]

items.title: Open SQLite
items.text: `sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=5)` then `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` for `orders` and `order_lines`. [high]

items.title: Read the whole file first
items.text: `csv.DictReader(delimiter=";")`. Rows are grouped by `order_id`, email is lower-cased and the discount code is upper-cased. The function returns a list, so one bad row rejects the whole file before anything is saved. [high]

items.title: Parse amounts
items.text: `Decimal(value.strip())`. A decimal comma (`12,50`) raises `decimal.InvalidOperation`. Since 49bc16d the comma is no longer replaced. [high]

items.title: Price
items.text: subtotal − discount (`DISCOUNTS` table) + VAT at the hard-coded `VAT_RATE = 0.20`, rounded once with HALF_UP to the cent. [high]

items.title: Upsert
items.text: One transaction per order: `INSERT OR REPLACE` into `orders` with `total_cents = int(total * 100)`, then delete and re-insert its `order_lines`. Re-importing a file overwrites the orders. [high]

items.title: Finance reads the file
items.text: The SQLite file is copied nightly to the finance share. Finance sums `orders.total_cents` per day. [med]

items.title: After the DB write, read the file again
items.text: Once `import_file` finishes, the CLI parses the CSV a second time and sends one receipt per order in the file. It keeps no record of what was sent. [high]

items.title: Settings reloaded per receipt
items.text: `send_receipt` calls `load_settings()` again for every order. [high]

items.title: POST to the mail API
items.text: `requests.post(mail_api_url, json={to, template: receipt, order_id, total}, headers={Authorization: Bearer …})`. There is no `timeout`. [high]

items.title: First failure stops the loop
items.text: `raise_for_status()` raises. The remaining receipts are not sent, but the orders are already saved. [high]

items.title: Container starts the server
items.text: `serve --port 8080` → `Handler.db_path = db_path`; `ThreadingHTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", port))`. [high]

items.title: Route by prefix, no auth
items.text: `/health` → `{status: ok}`. Any path starting with `/orders/` uses the rest of the path as the id, query string included. There is no authentication. [high]

items.title: Connect per request
items.text: `storage.connect` runs the schema script on every request. If the file is missing, it creates an empty DB, so every lookup returns 404 instead of an error. [high]

items.title: Two SELECTs
items.text: Order row plus its lines. [high]

items.title: Shape the response
items.text: `total = total_cents / 100` (a float). The JSON includes `customer_email`. [high]

blocks.title: 4. Finance report: CSV → HTML on stdout

items.title: Read the CSV, not the DB
items.text: `report` parses the export file again. It never reads the SQLite totals that finance uses. [high]

items.title: Per-order columns by name
items.text: `getattr(pricing, f"{kind}_total")` for discount, vat and order. Discount and VAT are not rounded (e.g. `1.998`). [high]

items.title: Adjustments
items.text: Sums every row's `amount` from the adjustments CSV. It ignores the file's `day` column and fails on a decimal comma. [high]

items.title: Render
items.text: `jinja2.Template(TEMPLATE)` with no autoescape. `--day` only sets the heading; orders are not filtered by day. [high]

sections.title: Surprises
sections.intro: Places where the code, the docs and the runtime evidence disagree.

items.title: The daily import has failed since 2026-10-02: decimal commas no longer parse
items.evidence: 49bc16d (2026-09-30, "simplify amount parsing") dropped `.replace(",", ".")` and deleted `test_decimal_comma`, so CI stayed green. The change was deployed with c376ea1 on 2026-10-01 18:05. The 06:00 runs on 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-03 exited with 1 on `decimal.InvalidOperation` (logs/acme-orders.log:10, :29). The export has `12,50` and `8,00` on order A-1045 and dots on other rows. `read_orders` builds the full list before saving, so the whole file is rejected. Orders from 2026-10-01 on are missing from the DB, from the API, and from finance's sums. [high] The log copy ends 2026-10-03, so the current state is unknown.
items.fix: Restore comma handling in `parse_amount` and restore the deleted test. Re-import the missed files; the upsert makes this safe, but only without `--notify`. Alert on non-zero cron exit.

items.title: VAT rate is configurable on paper only
items.evidence: README.md:15 and acme.yaml.example:3 offer `ACME_VAT_RATE` / `vat_rate`, and `config.py:28` reads it into `Settings.vat_rate`. Nothing reads that field. `pricing.vat_total` uses the constant `VAT_RATE = Decimal("0.20")`. [high]
items.fix: Either pass the setting into pricing or remove it from config and README. A rate change alters `total_cents`, so tell finance first (docs/finance-export.md:6).

items.title: The finance report ignores its day, sums a month of adjustments, and crashes on the adjustments file
items.evidence: `--day` is only rendered into the `<h1>` (report.py:8, :37). Every order in the CSV is listed. `read_adjustments` sums every row and never reads the `day` column of `data/adjustments-2026-10.csv`, which holds one month. That file has `-8,40`, so `Decimal()` raises. The report reads the CSV, not the DB totals finance uses. Discount and VAT columns are unrounded. [high]
items.fix: Decide with finance whether the report or `total_cents` is the number of record. Filter orders and adjustments by day, and share one amount parser with the importer.

items.title: Receipts: no timeout, no dedupe, partial sends
items.evidence: `requests.post` has no `timeout`, so a hung mail API hangs the import job. `import --notify` re-sends a receipt for every order in the file on every run (cli.py:30). Re-importing to recover from the first finding would mail customers twice. The first HTTP error stops the loop after the DB is already written. [high]
items.fix: Add a timeout, record sent receipts (e.g. a column or table), and make the notify loop continue and report failures.

items.title: Order API is unauthenticated, binds all interfaces and returns customer emails
items.evidence: `ThreadingHTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", port))` with no auth check. The response includes `customer_email` (personal data). docs/api.md calls it read-only, but each request runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, and a wrong `ACME_DB_PATH` silently creates an empty DB. [high] Whether a proxy or network rule protects it is not in the repo.
items.fix: Confirm what sits in front of it (open question). Otherwise add auth, and open the DB read-only (`file:…?mode=ro`, `uri=True`).

items.title: Old pins likely break on Python 3.12, and lazy imports hide it
items.evidence: Jinja2 2.x imports `soft_unicode`, which MarkupSafe ≥2.1 removed, and nothing pins MarkupSafe, so `report` likely fails with ImportError on a fresh install [med]. requests 2.19.1 pulls urllib3 1.23, whose vendored `six` may not import on 3.12 [guess]. Known advisories: PyYAML 5.3.1 `FullLoader` (CVE-2020-14343, used at config.py:23) and requests <2.20 keeping the `Authorization` header on https→http redirects (CVE-2018-18074) [med]. CI never imports these paths.
items.fix: Run the dependency-audit skill. Bump to Jinja2 3, requests ≥2.32 and PyYAML ≥6 with `safe_load`. Add a smoke test that imports every module.

items.title: No .dockerignore: `COPY . .` bakes local data into the image
items.evidence: `.gitignore` excludes `data/`, `logs/`, `*.db`, `acme.yaml`, but Docker does not read it. This working copy has `data/` (order CSVs with customer emails) and `logs/`. Both would end up in an image built here. [high]

items.title: Orders stored before 2026-08-05 may hold truncated cents
items.evidence: Until 7a9f245 `order_total` was not rounded: VAT was rounded but a 10% discount could leave three decimals. `int(total * 100)` truncates rather than rounds. Rows from that period that were never re-imported can be one cent low. [med]
items.fix: Round explicitly in `save_order` (`_round(total) * 100`), and ask finance whether old rows need a recompute.

items.title: Report HTML is rendered without autoescape
items.evidence: `jinja2.Template(...)` defaults to `autoescape=False`. `order_id` from the shop CSV goes into the HTML as-is. [high]

items.title: Renaming a pricing function breaks the report without a grep hit
items.evidence: `getattr(pricing, f"{kind}_total")` reaches `discount_total`, `vat_total` and `order_total` through a built string, so a plain search for `vat_total(` misses this caller. [high]
items.fix: Call the three functions directly, or keep the names fixed.

items.title: Production runs from a source checkout through a cron the repo does not contain
items.evidence: The traceback paths are `/srv/acme-orders/src/acme_orders/…`, not site-packages, so the cron import does not use the Docker image (which runs `pip install .`). Deploys are logged as `cron deploy <sha>`. None of this is in the repo or the README. [med]
items.fix: Document the scheduler and the deploy step in the README, or move them into the repo.
